correctness.rationale: For finite connected simple graph with positive lengths, r<epsilon=min ell_e means same-edge sample pairs contribute exactly 2r/ell_e-r²/ell_e²; two different incident edges contribute r²/(2ell_e ell_f) conditioned on their orientation; nonincident pairs require traversing a full intermediate edge and contribute zero. Therefore F_p(r)=2rΣp_e²/ell_e+r²[-Σp_e²/ell_e²+Σ_incident p_e p_f/(ell_e ell_f)]. A pure-edge probe yields slope 2/ell_e. A half-half pair probe has quadratic coefficient b=-1/(4ell_e²)-1/(4ell_f²)+I_ef/(4ell_e ell_f), so 4ell_e ell_f b+ell_f/ell_e+ell_e/ell_f=I_ef, reconstructing each named length and the edge-indexed line graph. Classical Whitney line-graph reconstruction yields abstract graph uniquely except K3 versus K1,3, and strong lifting of named edges for ≥5 vertices. Triangle and claw with identical edge lengths have the same local coefficient formula for every mixture; different Betti numbers show intrinsic nonhomeomorphism. Verified boundary m=1 and r below min length; positive exact population germs essential. The five-graph independent coordinate integration check.py corroborates only finite examples.
